name: City Council Meeting Agenda
agenda_text:
SUSAN McSWEENEY  BRAD HALPERN  RAY PEARL  NED E DAVIS  KELLY HONIG
  Mayor  Mayor Pro Tem  Councilmember  Councilmember  Councilmember

  AGENDA
  Regular Meeting of the City Council
  CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE
  City Council Chambers
  31200 Oak Crest Drive
  Westlake Village, CA 91361

  WEDNESDAY, MARCH 11, 2026 - 6:30 p.m.
  .

  ATTEND OR WATCH THE MEETING
  Members of the public may attend in-person in the Council Chambers or watch the meeting
  through Zoom, City Website (Live Stream) or Cable TV Channel 10. City Council Chamber doors
  open 30 minutes before the meeting start time.

  PUBLIC COMMENT/SPEAKERS
  Members of the public may express comments to the City Council in person at the meeting or
  may submit written comments before or at the meeting. Submit a Public Speaker card or Written
  Comment card to the City Clerk prior to the public comment portion of that item. Public speakers
  are limited to three minutes unless the presiding officer sets a different limit for meeting
  management purposes. An oral summary of written comments may be given at the discretion of
  the presiding officer.

  Written comments may be emailed to the City Clerk's Office at cityclerk@wlv.org no later than
  4:00 p.m. on the meeting date. Written comments will be provided to City Council prior to the
  meeting and posted at https://www.wlv.org/569/City-Council-Supplemental-Packets

  ZOOM VIEWING ONLY:
  Members of the public watching through Zoom will not have the ability to provide comments on
  agenda items. Zoom is offered strictly as an additional viewing platform. To provide comments,
  see Public Comments/Speakers section.

  https://us02web.zoom.us/j/84070910557
  Webinar ID: 840 7091 0557
  One-tap Mobile:
  +16469313860,,84070910557# OR +13017158592,,84070910557#
  Telephone:
  +1 669 900 9128 OR +1 646 931 3860 OR +1 301 715 8592
 Unless the City Council holds a teleconference meeting under AB 2449 (2022) guidelines, the
meeting will not be cancelled if technical issues occur.

In accordance with the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990, if you require a disability-related
modification or accommodation to attend or participate in this meeting, including auxiliary aids or
services, please call the City Clerk’s office at (818) 706-1613 at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

Any disclosable public records related to an open session item on a regular meeting agenda and
distributed by the City to the City Council less than 72 hours prior to that meeting are available for
public inspection at City Hall (31200 Oak Crest Drive, Westlake Village) during normal business
hours and are posted on the City’s Website - https://www.wlv.org/569/City-Council-Supplemental-
Packets.

CALL TO ORDER: 6:30 p.m.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE:

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Honig, Davis, Pearl, Mayor Pro Tem Halpern,
  Mayor McSweeney,

APPROVAL OF AGENDA:
APPROVAL OF MINUTES:

Minutes of February 25, 2026 City Council Regular Meeting

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS/CEREMONIAL MATTERS:

1.  Volunteer Appreciation – Recognition of 2025 City Volunteers

PUBLIC COMMENTS:
Members of the public may address the City Council on non-agenda items that are within the Council’s
subject matter jurisdiction. Please observe the time limit (three minutes unless a different limit is set by the
presiding officer for meeting management purposes). Public Comments may be presented via a written
comment, see Page 1 for deadline. Complete a Speaker Card and submit it to the City Clerk to be called
to speak while in the Council Chambers.

COUNCIL RESPONSE:

STAFF COMMENTS:

COUNCIL COMMENTS:

CITY COUNCIL COMMITTEE REPORTS: Reports on City Council Committee meetings held.

1.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE REPORT – PURE WATER PROJECT TRAFFIC
  CONTROL UPDATE - City Council to receive updated traffic control phasing
  concepts and provide comments.
 2.  PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE REPORT – SPEED LIMITS – To provide direction
  to staff.

PUBLIC HEARINGS: None

CONSENT CALENDAR: Matters listed under the Consent Calendar are considered to be routine and
will be enacted by one motion and one vote. Unless otherwise requested by a Councilmember, there will
be no separate discussion of these items. If discussion is desired, that item will be removed from the
Consent Calendar and will be considered separately.

  APPROVAL OF WARRANTS: Warrants effective March 1, 2026 in the amount of
  $673,463.56

  GENERAL BUSINESS:

  1.  GRANT FUNDING APPROPRIATION AND UPDATE ON PLAYGROUND
  EQUIPMENT AND PLAY AREA SURFACE INSTALLATION AT
  BERNIECE BENNETT PARK; PLAYGROUND CLOSURE DATES -
  Receive and file the update regarding the Berniece Bennett Park
  Playground Rehabilitation Project and temporary play area closure;
  determine that the project remains exempt from CEQA; and appropriate
  $183,072 in Proposition 68 grant funding for the project.

OLD BUSINESS:

1.  AWARD OF CONTRACT TO R DEPENDABLE CONSTRUCTION INC FOR THE
  CITY HALL RESTROOM REHABILITATION PROJECT – PHASE I AND
  REJECTION OF BID PROTEST - Reject the bid protest by Ambit Construction &
  Design, Inc., award a construction contract for the installation of the City Hall
  Restroom Rehabilitation Project, Phase I, to R Dependable Construction Inc in the
  amount of $85,900.00, determine that the project is exempt from CEQA, authorize
  the City Manager to approve change orders up to the 10% contingency amount,
  and authorize the Mayor to sign and execute the construction contract on behalf
  of the City.

2.  CLEAN POWER ALLIANCE OF SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA ELECTRIC FLEET
  TRANSITION PROGRAM – AUTHORIZATION TO PURCHASE ELECTRIC
  TRUCK - Authorize spending up to $70,000 to purchase a new 2025 Ford F150
  Lightning Truck as part of the Clean Power Alliance Electric Fleet Transition
  Program Agreement and approve the Mayor to execute all agreements.

NEW BUSINESS:

1.  FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 ASSESSMENTS FOR LIGHTING AND LANDSCAPE
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICTS: RESOLUTION NUMBERS 2440-26 THROUGH
  2445-26 - Approving the Engineer’s Reports and setting a Public Hearing of
  public protests of the Districts to be held at the April 22, 2026 City Council
  meeting and that the City Clerk be directed to give notice of the Public Hearing.
   RESOLUTION NO. 2440-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE INITIATING PROCEEDINGS FOR THE LEVY AND
  COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS WITHIN CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE
  LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1 FOR FISCAL YEAR
  2026-27, ORDERING THE PREPARATION OF AN ENGINEER’S REPORT AND
  APPROVING SUCH REPORT PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF
  DIVISION 15 OF THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

  RESOLUTION NO. 2441-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO LEVY AND COLLECT
  WITHIN CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE LIGHTING MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT
  DISTRICT NO. 1 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
  PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE AND
  APPOINTING A TIME AND PLACE FOR HEARING PROTESTS

  RESOLUTION NO. 2442-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE INITIATING PROCEEDINGS FOR THE LEVY AND
  COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS WITHIN CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE LIGHTING
  MAINTENANCE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27,
  ORDERING THE PREPARATION OF AN ENGINEER’S REPORT AND APPROVING
  SUCH REPORT PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF
  THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

  RESOLUTION NO. 2443-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO LEVY AND COLLECT
  ASSESSMENTS WITHIN WESTLAKE VILLAGE LANDSCAPE MAINTENANCE
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 1 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 PURSUANT TO THE
  PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE
  AND APPOINTING A TIME AND PLACE FOR HEARING PROTESTS

  RESOLUTION NO. 2444-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY
  OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE INITIATING PROCEEDINGS FOR THE LEVY AND
  COLLECTION OF ASSESSMENTS WITHIN WESTLAKE SPECTRUM LOCAL
  LANDSCAPE ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 15 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27,
  ORDERING THE PREPARATION OF AN ENGINEER'S REPORT AND APPROVING
  SUCH REPORT PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF
  THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE

  RESOLUTION NO. 2445-26: A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL
  OF THE CITY OF WESTLAKE VILLAGE DECLARING ITS INTENTION TO LEVY AND
  COLLECT ASSESSMENTS WITHIN WESTLAKE SPECTRUM LOCAL LANDSCAPE
  ASSESSMENT DISTRICT NO. 15 FOR FISCAL YEAR 2026-27 PURSUANT TO THE
  PROVISIONS OF PART 2 OF DIVISION 15 OF THE STREETS AND HIGHWAYS CODE
  AND APPOINTING A TIME AND PLACE FOR HEARING PROTESTS

2.  REVIEW OF ENCROACHMENT PERMIT FEES - Direct staff to prepare an
  Encroachment Permit Fee Resolution incorporating the proposed fee adjustments
  for City Council adoption at a future City Council meeting.
 ADJOURNMENT:

This agenda was posted on Friday, March 6, 2026 at 4:30 p.m. on the City’s website and
in the Posting Board at City Hall.

  Deputy City Clerk
  March 6, 2026
